chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskān, from Ya'qub al-Bazzāz, who said:

I said to him: 'I rise a little before dawn and pray four rak'at, then I fear that dawn will break — should I begin with the Witr or complete the rak'at?' He said: 'No, rather perform the Witr and delay the four rak'at until you complete them in the early part of the day.'

key_terms.اَلْوَتْرُ: Witr (the odd-numbered prayer concluding the night prayer)
key_terms.صَدْرُ اَلنَّهَارِ: The early part of the day (morning)

ai.seo_question: What is the preferred order for night prayer if dawn is approaching: Witr first or the four voluntary rak'at?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, the Imam clarifies the flexibility in arranging night prayers, prioritizing the completion of Witr before Fajr to ensure its distinct identity is not lost in the dawn light. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on preserving the specific timing and order of supererogatory acts while accommodating practical concerns, such as the fear of dawn breaking unexpectedly. It underscores the principle that voluntary prayers can be adjusted in sequence to maintain their ritual integrity without compromising the obligatory Fajr prayer.
